setup: Start standing, bar taken from a rack or the floor
Feet hip width, hands just outside your thighs
Soften your knees and keep that bend
Shoulders back, brace before each rep
execution: Push your hips back, not down
Slide the bar down your thighs
Stop before your back starts to round
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall
faults: Don't bend your knees more on the way down
Don't round your lower back to reach lower
Don't let the bar drift away from your legs
Don't lean back at the top

notes: Your back position sets the depth, not the floor. A typical end point is the bar just below the knee; go only as low as your back stays flat.
Starting from a rack set at mid-thigh height saves pulling the bar off the floor for every set.
If you lift the bar from the floor, use a proper deadlift with a flat back to get it to the start position.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dumbbell RDL
regressions.reason: Lighter and easier to set up; same hinge.

regressions.name: Cable pull-through
regressions.reason: Same hips-back pattern with the load pulling from behind; easier on the grip.

regressions.name: Dowel hip hinge
regressions.reason: Teaches hips back with a flat back before adding load.

progressions.name: Deficit RDL
progressions.reason: Standing on a low step adds range; only if the back stays flat at the bottom.

progressions.name: Single-leg RDL
progressions.reason: One side at a time, with more balance demand.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell RDL
substitutions.reason: Same hinge; load is each dumbbell, so numbers are not comparable.

substitutions.name: Cable pull-through
substitutions.reason: Hip hinge on a cable when no bar is free.

substitutions.name: 45° back extension
substitutions.reason: Hinge for glutes and hamstrings with less load in the hands.

substitutions.name: Seated leg curl
substitutions.reason: Hamstrings with no hinge; a knee-bending movement instead.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view, figure facing right, camera at hip height, whole body in frame. No rack.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall with knees softly bent (about 15°). Arms straight, bar hanging against the upper thighs with an overhand grip just outside the legs. Shoulders back, spine neutral, feet flat about hip width.

keyPositions.label: Knee level
keyPositions.describe: Hips pushed back and torso leaning forward. Bar sliding down the thighs to just above the knees. Knee bend unchanged, shins near vertical, spine still neutral.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Torso about 15° above horizontal. Bar just below the knees, no lower than mid-shin. Back flat, neck in line with the spine. Shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Knee bend the same as at the start. Hips well behind the heels.

guideBrief.barPath: Vertical over mid-foot, touching or within about 1 cm of the legs; drift ≤ 3% of body height
emphasise: Hips move back while the knee angle barely changes
Bar stays in contact with the legs
Back angle held flat from start to bottom
doNotShow: Knees bending more as the bar lowers (turning it into a squat)
